definition: Data backup and disaster recovery preserve data, applications or digital systems and enable them to be restored following disruption or failure. Counts when the project finances, procures, establishes or explicitly requires backup systems, replication, failover, recovery environments, geographically separate recovery sites or defined technical recovery objectives. The defining intervention concerns recovery of data, applications or computing services; alternative communications paths belong to network_redundancy, backup electricity belongs to backup_power, and physical protection belongs to resilient_infrastructure_design. Organizational continuity planning alone does not count unless it includes a specific technical backup or recovery mechanism. Does not count for physical reconstruction, community recovery, general emergency response, routine data storage or generic statements about continuity or reliability. "Backup" with no object counts here only when the paragraph is about data or systems. Links between a data centre and its recovery site are disaster recovery.
boundary: The project protects or restores data, applications or computing services after failure.
